bindings.label: A 32-year-old woman had painless unilateral blurring of vision in her left eye for the past three months

Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in the right eye and 20/250 in the left eye; color vision and Humphrey visual field analysis 24-2 were normal in the right eye, while the left eye exhibited severely depressed fields with central 10 degrees around fixation preserved

Right eye examination was normal with a cup disc ratio of 0.5; left eye showed engorged episcleral vessels, a relative afferent pupillary defect, grade III nuclear sclerosis with cortical cataract, and a cup disc ratio of 0.9 on fundus examination
Intraocular pressure was 16 mmHg in the right eye and 42 mmHg in the left eye by Goldman applanation tonometry; gonioscopy indicated open angles in both eyes
There was no proptosis or audible bruit, and extraocular movements were full
Neuroimaging was negative, with no evidence of intracranial mass or vascular malformation
The radiologist recommends initiating intraocular pressure-lowering therapy for the left eye
